subject: design-technology
title: Foundations: Levers and Linkages
welcome_lead: Grab a spanner and see how levers and linkages turn small forces and motions into big results.
meta_desc: Learn the three classes of lever and basic linkage types for GCSE D&T.
final_note: You can classify levers and recognise linkage types in everyday products.

concepts.def: Rigid bar that pivots about a fulcrum.
Set of bars joined to change direction of motion.

walkthroughs.body_html: A 1st class lever has the fulcrum in the middle — like scissors. A 2nd class has the load in the middle — like a wheelbarrow. A 3rd class has the effort in the middle — like tweezers or a fishing rod. Each gives a different mechanical advantage.

A reverse motion linkage flips input direction; a parallel motion linkage keeps two bars parallel as they move; a bell crank turns motion through 90 degrees. Pop-up books rely on simple linkages to bring images to life.
A crowbar 1 m long has the fulcrum 100 mm from the load. Effort arm = 900 mm, load arm = 100 mm, so mechanical advantage = 9. Pushing with 50 N lifts a 450 N load.
